chapter_title: Concerning the First Man and the Ambassador and the Ship; what they resemble.
chapter_note: This kephalaion is largely a string of redemption-similes (First Man, ship of day/Great Spirit, Living Spirit, Ambassador). The main late material is the dialogue-attribution opening in ¶1 and the final direct exhortation to the disciples in ¶6 (application/pastoral voice).

paragraphs.core_text: The First [Man] is like a great distinguished man whose treasure has been taken away from him. He came to pursue his treasure. This is how the [First] Man too came after his sons from the heights, so that he might redeem them and retrieve his treasure, which had been scattered amongst his enemies.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue-attribution frame: "Once again he speaks:" (hagiographic/editorial speaker formula).
paragraphs.temporal_note: The simile itself is teaching about the First Man’s descent/redemption (cosmic beings and soteriological mechanics), but the explicit speaker-attribution is later Kephalaia frame.

paragraphs.core_text: Once again, [he is like a man] whose two sons were taken away from him by [ ... He] came out toward them to redeem them. Again, this is how the First Man [ ... ] shines in the heights because of his two sons, who were separated from him. They are his living soul that exist in two powers, which makes four.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmological exposition framed as a simile; no institutional/present-day application, and the content stays within the Manichaean redemption system (First Man, living soul, powers). Some uncertainty remains because the parable style may reflect Mani’s pedagogical redaction rather than the oldest schematic substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: Once again, the ship [of the day] is like a great spear [ ... ... The Great Spirit too, which is in it, is like a wise [crafts]man who might beautify and set aright [all] the armour for war.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic-entity mapping (ship of day; Great Spirit) with correspondential simile language; no exhortation/citation/institutional anchoring.

paragraphs.core_text: Once again, the Living Spirit is like a combatant who might go towards a king's son who has been taken prisoner of war, and he redeems him from the hands of his enemies.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal teaching via simile describing a redemption function (Living Spirit as redeemer) within the cosmic drama; no late ecclesial application markers.

paragraphs.core_text: [The Amba]ssador too is like a great man [ ... ] because of the treasure [ ... ] hand of his prisoners [ ... ] these light powers [ ... ... the] sons and their soul, so that they would [ ... ... (the soul) might] be brought forth in the land wherein it was imprisoned.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Soteriological mechanics centered on the Ambassador and the extraction of the soul/light from imprisonment; despite lacunae, it remains cosmological and non-institutional.

Direct second-person exhortation (“You yourselves must…”) addressed to disciples, aiming at purification and future reward; this is application/pastoral voice rather than impersonal cosmological exposition, and fits the chapter’s end-weighted editorial drift.
